title: Pakistan Marks 61st Defence Day, Leadership Invokes Last Year's 'Marka-e-Haq' Conflict With India
detail: Pakistan observed its 61st Defence and Martyrs' Day on September 6, 2026, commemorating the 1965 war with India. President Asif Ali Zardari said the day 'provides us with an opportunity to pay tribute to the immortal sacrifices of the brave sons of the nation,' while Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said 'the entire nation is proud of our brave Pakistan Army, Pakistan Air Force and Pakistan Navy.' Both leaders explicitly linked the commemoration to last year's four-day military confrontation with India (which Pakistan calls 'Marka-e-Haq' and the 'Bunyanum Marsoos' operation), with Sharif saying the response Pakistan's armed forces delivered under Field Marshal Asim Munir's leadership 'will be remembered for generations' and Zardari calling it a chapter that 'added another glorious chapter to our national history.' Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmad Babar Sidhu and Naval Chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf led the military's own tributes via ISPR, with Munir calling September 6 'an enduring symbol of national unity, courage and resolve.' The remarks were commemorative and domestically-focused; no new operational threat or troop movement toward India was announced, and India's government did not issue an on-record response.

confidenceReason: On-record statements from Pakistan's president, PM and military leadership confirmed by two Tier-2 Pakistani outlets (Dawn, Express Tribune).
